_comment: Purely visual world tuning. Dressing never collides, receives touches or participates in raycasts. All gameplay geometry remains in maps/*.json.

groundMarking._layerStepMetres: Ground markings overlap at bends and cross each other. Two faces on one plane shimmer as the camera moves, so each marking and each segment sits a few millimetres off its neighbours. tools/check-zfight verifies it.

foliage._comment: Keep shadows on trunks, canopy tiers, crowns and rocks. Small undergrowth and moss add thousands of shadow casters and no useful depth at walking distance. Part names must match World/Foliage.luau -- a rename here silently stops a canopy casting.
foliage._shadowRadiusMetres: How close a plant has to be to somewhere the player can stand before it casts a shadow, measured to a trail centreline or to one of the open areas the scatter carves out -- the clearing, the barn apron, the pond, the west corridor and every gate. shadowParts decides WHICH parts of a plant can cast; this decides whether that plant is near enough to be worth it.
foliage._shadowRadiusMeasured: Hub shadow casters against this radius, from tools/foliage-report: no radius 5784, 26 m 4870, 20 m 4005, 16 m 3154, 12 m 1993, 10 m 1411. Twelve is a 66% cut for shadows that were landing behind other trees. Raise it if the treeline reads flat; lower it if the hub is heavy on a low-end device. Delete the field and every plant casts, which is what it did before.

treeLine._crownTiers: A stepped spire: stacked cylinder discs tapering to a tip, the same silhouette the hub's conifers use. The border treeline was two spheres on a stick -- the 'trees are blobs' read the hub was rebuilt once to fix, where the fix never reached the field borders. widthFraction scales crownWidthMetres; thicknessFraction and positionFraction scale the tree's own height. Alternating tiers take the lighter pine tone, which gives the canopy depth without a second material. Costs parts and no shadows -- border scenery never casts.

_fonts: World signage, resolved by Shared/Fonts with a fallback. Every name here was checked against Enum.Font on 2026-09-07. Oswald is condensed and reads like a painted sign board; PermanentMarker is for the things a person actually wrote by hand -- chalk price lists, flyers on the corkboard; RobotoMono is for the leaderboard, because times only line up in columns if the digits are the same width.

budget._comment: Render budgets, checked by tools/check-budget. Deliberately a little above what is measured today: a tripwire for a regression, not a target to fill.
budget._shadowCasters: Worth far more than a part under Future lighting with global shadows. The hub was casting 5784 of them, most landing behind other trees; presentation.foliage.shadowRadiusMetres is what brought it down.
budget._transparentSquareMetres: Semi-transparent surfaces cannot early-out of the depth test, so a 132 x 20 m boundary wall at 0.2 alpha forces overdraw across much of the screen. Area is the cost, not part count.
budget._measured:
Where the headroom went, at the time these were set. Fields: parts Holdfast 506, Speedball and Woods 383; shadow casters Speedball 184, Holdfast 90; transparent area Speedball 1246 m2 (its netting, which has to be see-through), Holdfast 900, Woods 308. Woods and Holdfast were at 5729 and 13220 m2 of alpha before their boundary walls stopped being semi-transparent.

The Landing: 8615 parts and 2548 casters for everything, of which 7579 parts and 2012 casters are foliage -- so the barn, gates, board and six people are about a thousand parts and five hundred casters, all of them close to the player and worth it. Hub foliage was casting 5784 before shadowRadiusMetres.
